instruction.text: A crate of 12 bottles of milk has a mass of 6.3 kilograms. The empty crate has a mass of 300 grams. What is the mass of each bottle of milk?

atoms.b: Mass of all the milk bottles: <mat><gap>6300</gap>g-<gap>300</gap>g=<gap>6000</gap></mat>g
Therefore, the mass of one milk bottle is 500g.

instruction.text: Jasmin spends £1,886.59 in the shop. She buys a set of 12 chairs. She also buys a measuring jug for £2.59. How much did Jasmin spend on each chair?

atoms.b: Therefore, Jasmin spent £<mat><gap>157</gap></mat> on each chair.

instruction.text: The school needs to buy some brownies for sports day. There are 5 year groups, all with 104 pupils. The school wants to buy enough for one brownie each. The bakery sells brownies in boxes of 12. How many boxes should the school buy?

atoms.b: Therefore, the school needs to buy <mat><gap>44</gap></mat> boxes of brownies.

instruction.text: Pencils are sold in boxes. A box contains 16 packs of pencils. A pack contains 6 pencils. A school would like to buy 3,500 pencils. How many boxes should the school buy?

atoms.b: Number of pencils in a box: <mat><gap>16 6</gap>*<gap>16 6</gap>=</mat>
Therefore, the school should buy <mat><gap>37</gap></mat> boxes of pencils.
